coaching.metaTitle: Life coaching — sessions, formats and pricing — Fareed Quraishi
coaching.metaDescription: One-to-one life coaching for career transitions and finding direction. What sessions involve, online or in person, and what the coaching costs.

intro.eyebrow: Life coaching · One-to-one · Online and in person
intro.title: Life coaching that starts from your life as it actually is.
intro.lede: I work with people who are navigating a transition, carrying more than feels sustainable, or who have built a life that looks right from the outside and no longer fits from within. The work is not to become someone else. It is to get clearer about what you want, and to build enough capacity to move toward it.

who.title: Who coaching is for
who.intro: People arrive from very different lives, but there is a recognisable shape to the ones who get the most from this work.
items: You are in the middle of a career transition — chosen or not — and the next step is not obvious.
You have built a life that looks successful, and find it hard to feel satisfied inside it.
Something has started to give: work, caregiving, study, or ambition has crowded out the rest.
You understand your patterns well, and are frustrated that insight alone has not changed them.
You are circling a decision and cannot tell which of your impulses is actually yours.
You want more from the next stage of life, and cannot yet say what that would be.
You notice that rest, closeness, or uncertainty registers in your body as pressure rather than safety.
who.note: You do not need a diagnosis, a clear goal, or a convincing account of what is wrong. A vague sense that something is not working is enough to begin.

explore.title: What we can explore together
explore.intro: There is no fixed curriculum. What we look at depends on where you are, and it changes as your life does.
items: What you want — including the parts you have a feeling about and no words for yet.
A transition, and what the next stage of your life could actually look like.
Patterns that repeat under pressure, and what each one has been protecting.
The shape of your week: load, recovery, and what has quietly become the whole of it.
Decisions you keep circling, and how to separate your own impulse from someone else’s.
Boundaries, closeness, and relationships that keep arriving at the same place.
Where participation is possible now, at the scale your life currently allows.

sessions.title: What one-to-one sessions are like
sessions.intro: There is no intake questionnaire and nothing to prepare. An hour, in conversation, following what is actually alive for you.

steps.name: Beginning
steps.body: We start with what brings you here, in whatever terms you can manage on the day.

steps.name: Exploration
steps.body: We look at the patterns, circumstances, and possibilities together, including what you have already tried and why it may not have held.

steps.name: Where it leaves you
steps.body: You leave with a useful direction, a question to sit with, or something small to try between sessions. Sometimes the honest next step is simply to keep talking.

sessions.note: No two sessions are identical, and I will not promise that any particular session produces a particular result.

format.title: Online and in person

items.name: Online
items.body: By video call, wherever you are. Flexible and accessible, and easy to fit around work, caregiving, or travel. Most sessions are held this way.

items.name: In person
items.body: Sessions are also available in person in the Kitchener–Waterloo area, when that is practical for both of us.

format.note: When practical, I encourage meeting in person. There is something valuable about sharing a space, slowing down, and being fully present with another person. That is a preference rather than a claim about outcomes — the coaching itself works the same way in either setting, and neither is the lesser choice.

practical.title: Session format and pricing
practical.intro: Set out plainly, so nothing about format or cost has to be guessed at.
practical.note: These are introductory prices, offered as part of the inaugural program.

start.title: How to get started
start.intro: Four steps, and you can stop at any of them.

steps.name: Send a request
steps.body: A short form: your name, an email address, which format interests you, and — if you want — a sentence about what you would like to be different. Nothing is booked by sending it.

steps.name: I reply personally
steps.body: Usually within three business days, with times for a 15-minute call. It comes straight to me, not to an assistant or an automated sequence.

steps.name: We speak for 15 minutes
steps.body: We introduce ourselves, talk about what you are looking for, and answer each other’s questions. It is a conversation about the work, not a coaching session.

steps.name: You decide
steps.body: If it is a good fit, I will send the practical terms in writing before anything is paid. If it is not, I will say so, and point you somewhere better suited if I can.

elsewhere.title: Where this work comes from
elsewhere.body: The coaching is grounded in Authentic Manifestation: a body of writing about nervous-system regulation, a viable day-to-day life, and the practice of participating in your own. You do not need to have read any of it to begin — it is there for anyone who wants the thinking in full.

scope.text: Coaching is personal development support. It is not psychotherapy, diagnosis, or medical treatment, and it does not replace them. Where what you bring would be better served by clinical care, I will say so plainly.
